title: CEEMDAN: ensemble averaging with adaptive noise
summary: CEEMDAN repeatedly estimates components from perturbed signals and updates a shared residual. The noise modes and ensemble averages are algorithmic inputs, not decorative uncertainty bands.

steps.title: Generate perturbations
steps.text: Normalize the input, draw seeded noise, and decompose the noise realizations.

steps.title: Average first IMFs
steps.text: Apply EMD to each perturbed input and average its first IMF.

steps.title: Update adaptively
steps.text: Perturb the current residual with the next noise mode, average local means, and extract the next cIMF.

steps.title: Retain the residue
steps.text: Continue until the stopping criterion, then retain the remaining signal for additive reconstruction.

parameters.name: trials
parameters.effect: Number of ensemble members; this small animation uses 8, while DeTime's default is 100.

parameters.name: epsilon
parameters.effect: Controls the perturbation scale; this visibility-oriented trace uses 0.04, not the default 0.005.

parameters.name: seed and n_jobs
parameters.effect: The trace uses seed 42 and serial execution. Preserve both for reproducibility.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Affects DeTime's grouping after the upstream component extraction.

cautions: Different CEEMDAN variants exist; PyEMD includes the later improved formulation documented by its authors.
An ensemble average does not establish that an IMF is a unique physical component.
Raw DeTime IMF arrays use (mode, time, channel), including a singleton channel for one series.
trace_note: Trial inputs, first IMFs, and adaptive local means recorded from EMD-signal 1.10.0; max_imf=3 bounds this upstream teaching run. DeTime's example below exposes the public controls and does not set this internal trace cap.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
